items.title: 'The price of food is ridiculous': Asylum seekers sent to Nauru by Australia say they are going hungry
items.description: According to a survey of 78 asylum seekers on Nauru, 99 per cent say they are regularly skipping meals because they cannot afford to buy enough food, while more than three quarters say they rarely have access to free, clean drinking water.

items.title: Rules to tighten on AI use in decision-making by government departments
items.description: Agencies like Centrelink and Services Australia will have to follow a framework to ensure decision-making is "fair and accurate" if they use AI.

items.title: Pauline Hanson 'not backing away' from controversial far-right interview
items.description: The One Nation leader was a guest on the podcast of controversial far-right UK figure Tommy Robinson, where she lamented the end of the White Australia policy.

items.title: Israel says Iran has launched missiles towards Jordan
items.description: The US warns its citizens to stay away from air and sea ports at Aqaba in southern Jordan, hours before Israeli authorities announced that Iranian missiles had been launched towards the city.

items.title: Antonelli extends F1 championship lead, heartbroken Russell crashes out in Belgium
items.description: Kimi Antonelli has extended his lead at the top of the F1 championship standings with victory in the Belgian Grand Prix, with Oscar Piastri overcoming an early knock and George Russell's race ending in heartbreak.

items.title: Actor Terence Donovan remembered by son Jason as 'larger than life'
items.description: Jason Donovan has paid tribute to his father who has died at the age of 90 after decades on Australian screens.

items.title: The 'terrifying' lab test results from store-bought bottle of vodka
items.description: Australia's bootleg booze market is booming and an alarming new discovery from a bottle of vodka sold in Melbourne reveals it is turning into a major health problem.

items.title: Russia pounds Kyiv in major ballistic missile attack
items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Russia battered Ukraine's capital Kyiv overnight into Sunday local time, with one of its biggest ballistic missile barrages of the war.

items.title: Argentina fans stage Times Square takeover ahead of World Cup final
items.description: Times Square has been the epicentre for World Cup celebrations throughout the tournament, but it reached new heights as Argentina fans swamped the "centre of the universe" ahead of the final against Spain in nearby New Jersey.

items.title: Andrew and Tristan Tate arrested on sex trafficking offences
items.description: British prosecutors say they are seeking the extradition of the Tate brothers from the US on rape and sex trafficking charges.

items.title: Bek never thought she would grow old until she left her church behind
items.description: Author Bek Condello says she has not spoken to her friends or family inside the church since she decided to leave.

items.title: Special guest dazzles aspiring astronauts at Space Day Out
items.description: Young Australians got one step closer to achieving their space exploration dreams on Sunday when they met a "real-life" astronaut.

items.title: There's anti-aging hype. Then there's the science showing real promise
items.description: The fear of aging is driving a wave of biohacking businesses promising to help restore youth and fight disease. Four Corners investigates the race to reverse the aging process.

items.title: Boys who embrace 'expansive masculinity' likely to fare better
items.description: These men are being the role models they never had. They hope to curb Australia's masculinity crisis.

items.title: Love story: Inseparable since meeting, these besties are planning retirement together
items.description: Tania Differding and Ella Crofts met as teenagers and have been inseparable since. The best friends, now aged 43, are planning the rest of their lives around one another.

items.title: Australia's only full-time penny-farthing maker is breaking world records
items.description: Farmer-turned-professional penny-farthing maker Dan Bolwell has a cult following of international enthusiasts.

items.title: Say goodbye Norma Jean because it's Spicks and Specks quiz time
items.description: Your spelling and general trivia skills are useless here. Settle into some pop culture nostalgia.

items.title: 'Why do you care how I choose to dress?': Boxer on critics of her hijab
items.description: Ahead of her professional debut, Tina Rahimi sat down for a lengthy interview about representation, the Islamophobia she encounters, and re-learning her identity after an Olympics heartbreak.

items.title: Curious case of absent US senator reignites elderly politicians debate
items.description: Washington's rumour mill is hyperactive at the best of times. But an elderly senator's lengthy absence from Congress is cranking it into frenzied overdrive.

items.title: Brondello suspended by WNBA for inappropriate comment
items.description: Australian coach Sandy Brondello apologises to WNBA star Angel Reese after she is suspended for one game by the league.

items.title: Hinkley set to coach Devils, Caddy taken to hospital as Dons end drought
items.description: Tasmania prepares to unveil Ken Hinkley as its inaugural AFL coach as Essendon snaps a 12-game losing streak despite losing Nate Caddy early.

items.title: Tom Trbojevic gutted after another injury, Titans, Dolphins record wins
items.description: The Dolphins shook off last week's humiliating thrashing to power past the Cowboys 36-16 at Lang Park, after Tom Trbojevic suffered another hamstring injury in Manly's defeat to Gold Coast.

items.title: Hundreds gather in Alice Springs ahead of Pine Gap protest
items.description: Hundreds of activists and academics have gathered in Alice Springs to join Arrernte traditional owners ahead of a planned protest against the joint Australian-US military base at Pine Gap.

items.title: Expert says new cyber law shows Vic government is out of touch with reality
items.description: Jacinta Allan is pledging nation-leading laws forcing tech giants to reveal the identity of trolls, and make it easier for parents to sue tech giants that cause psychiatric harm to their children.

items.title: Woman fighting for life after late-night crash south-east of Melbourne
items.description: A woman, aged in her 20s, has suffered life-threatening injuries after the car her family was in rolled into a drain at Catani.
